description: What the project must deliver. Functional and non-functional requirements with MoSCoW priority and lifecycle states (proposed, accepted, implemented, verified). The contract between intent and implementation.
title: Requirements

traces_to.description: Phase or task IDs that implement this

depends_on.description: IDs of other requirements this depends on

title.description: Short heading for the requirement, e.g. 'Continuidade operacional'. Optional: the May-era cohort has none.

maturity.description: What reality measures, in the operator's own six-state vocabulary (docs/OPERATOR_REQUIREMENTS.md). Distinct from `status`, which is what the operator DECIDED: a requirement can be accepted and parcial at once. Tokens are Portuguese because the table defining them is.

maturity_note.description: The justification paragraph carried verbatim from the source document, including any qualifier the enum cannot hold (R8: 'Parcial/Ausente por provedor.').

acceptance_criteria_preamble.description: The qualifier between 'Criterios de aceitacao.' and the bullets, when present (R3, R8, R12). Its own field because folding it into a bullet would corrupt a criterion and dropping it would silently make conditional criteria unconditional.

evidence.description: Markdown links to the documents that sustain the current maturity, verbatim.
